title: The House of Harrow Glen
premise: August Halloran, a skeptical property surveyor, arrives at Harrow Glen to appraise a decaying estate and discovers the mirrors lag one second behind reality — and in that stolen second, something else is looking back. The house was built by founders who bound a harvest entity into its walls with an unfinished ritual, sustained for two centuries by tenants who vanished. August, reluctantly allied with the caretaker's granddaughter Wren and a ghost of the first surveyor, must complete the ritual before the harvest moon rises — but finishing it demands a willing sacrifice to replace what the house has been feeding on. In the end, August offers themselves not as prey but as a new founder, rewriting the binding so the house feeds on memory instead of lives, and walks out hollowed but alive with Wren, who becomes their found family.
about_author: Mara Zhou is the pen name of a former land surveyor who spent a decade cataloguing properties no one wanted to buy. She writes horror about buildings that remember, and lives near the coast where the fog arrives on schedule.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: POV August. A cynical surveyor takes a lucrative job appraising Harrow Glen, a house that shouldn't exist on any deed. They measure rooms that don't match their own measurements. Emotional beat: professional detachment masking loneliness.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: POV August. The mirrors begin reflecting the room a beat behind; August blames faulty glass, then catches their reflection smiling after they've stopped. Emotional beat: rationality cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: The Caretaker's Granddaughter
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren Ashford confronts the stranger poking around her grandfather's house, warning them away from the east wing. She's been keeping the lights on and the doors shut since he disappeared. Emotional beat: guarded grief.

chapters.title: Inventory of Absences
chapters.summary: POV August. August finds the previous surveyor's notes in the walls — dated 1804, in their own handwriting style, ending mid-sentence. Emotional beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Deed Owes
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren reveals the house's history: every owner's lease ends at a harvest moon, every tenant unaccounted for. Her grandfather left her a key and one instruction: never finish anything you start here. Emotional beat: inherited fear becoming resolve.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: POV August. In the cellar, August deciphers the founders' ritual ledger — a binding meant to cage something the town fed to the house willingly, left incomplete when the last founder fled. Emotional beat: horror reframed as unfinished business.

chapters.title: Doors That Count
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The house rearranges overnight; hallways lengthen, exits subtract themselves. Wren realizes it's counting down, not keeping them in. Emotional beat: claustrophobia sharpening into urgency.

chapters.title: The Man in the Wallpaper
chapters.summary: POV August. August meets Elias Vane, the first surveyor, pressed into the plaster but still lucid. He explains the entity's hunger and warns that the ritual's final line requires 'a hand given freely.' Emotional beat: pity curdling into terror.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon Rising
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Nine days to the full moon. Wren and August form an uneasy pact; she knows the rituals, August can read the architecture. Emotional beat: two loners choosing trust.

chapters.title: Salt and Thresholds
chapters.summary: POV August. First attempt to seal the entity fails; the salt lines bloom like frost and the house retaliates by showing August their own future reflection, aged and wall-bound. Emotional beat: despair.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgot
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Research in village archives reveals the founders were the town's honored dead — and the town has been paying rent in missing persons ever since. Emotional beat: righteous anger at complicit silence.

chapters.title: A Room That Remembers You
chapters.summary: POV August. The nursery shows August a childhood they never had, tailored to keep them. They nearly stay. Wren drags them out by the collar. Emotional beat: temptation and rescue.

chapters.title: Elias's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Elias (interlude). The ghost recounts how he abandoned the ritual to save his own skin, dooming every tenant since. His guilt is the house's oldest brick. Emotional beat: shame seeking absolution.

chapters.title: Thirteen Steps Down
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The cellar grows a fourteenth step each night; beneath it, the entity stirs, wearing her grandfather's voice. She almost answers. Emotional beat: love weaponized against her.

chapters.title: The Price List
chapters.summary: POV August. Elias clarifies the cost: the ritual needs a founder's hand freely given — a life bound to the house forever. August quietly decides it will be theirs, without telling Wren. Emotional beat: self-sacrifice as penance for a life half-lived.

chapters.title: Storm Before the Moon
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Preparations: chalk circles, mirror-breaking, the ledger's instructions memorized. Wren catches August practicing goodbye and forces a promise: no secrets between family. Emotional beat: found family solidifying under pressure.

chapters.title: The House Opens Its Eyes
chapters.summary: POV August. Harvest eve. Every mirror reflects forward now — showing the moonrise before it happens. The house stops pretending to be a house. Emotional beat: awe and terror indivisible.

chapters.title: Ritual of the Founders
chapters.summary: POV alternating August/Wren. At moonrise they run the rite through the shifting halls, Elias holding doors open with his ghost-weight, the entity tearing through walls behind them. Emotional beat: desperate momentum.

chapters.title: The Hand Given Freely
chapters.summary: POV August. At the threshold stone, August offers their hand — but speaks new terms, binding the house to feed on memory rather than flesh, naming Wren heir. The entity accepts because consent, not blood, is the old law. Emotional beat: courage redefining the price.

chapters.title: What August Forgot
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The payment taken: August loses whole years — their childhood, their mother's face. They walk out alive, hollow-eyed, asking who they are. Wren answers: mine. Emotional beat: grief braided with devotion.

chapters.title: Deed Transferred
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The house settles, mirrors honest again, Elias released into light. Wren signs herself in as the new keeper with August as co-founder — the first entry the ledger accepts gladly. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, written by hand.

chapters.title: Harrow Glen, Appraised
chapters.summary: POV August. Months later, August returns to finish the appraisal, memory slowly regrowing like scar tissue. The house holds warmth now. Final line: some houses are worth exactly what you pay for them. Emotional beat: hard-won peace.
